element.namespace_address: dotted namespace address. Element: An element is any nameable part of an entity as a type; however, just because an element can be named doesn't mean it is interesting, remarkable, or deserving of special attention. Many elements can be immediately seen, or are easily inferred. Entity: An entity is a whole, independent thing with its own distinct existence, while an element is a smaller part or component that makes up that whole. All entities are elements, but not all elements are entities. Entity or an element depends entirely on your level of abstraction (your scope). The moment you zoom into a component and examine its internal composition, that component transitions conceptually from a passive "element" into an active "entity" with its own subordinate elements. NS, Namespace Scope: The scope of the Artifact Type. The five base valid types are code, document, media, data, and stakeholder. AT, Artifact Type: This is a general category or classification that groups individual artifacts together based on shared characteristics. Artifact Types can be used to anneal or combine many of the same type of AUE into types (for example photos, data objects, scripts, templates, etc). Parametric: A quality or quantity that can be tuned but does not carry a specific name in the scope of the namespace of this AUE. We do not name parametrics with a namespace address in this graph or as part of this operation.
element.role: AUE, Artifact Under Examination: The entity (thing or things) being examined, created, or used. Artifacts can include photographs, contracts, stories, resale assets, and software. The work can concern multiple artifacts and projects. Whether an AUE serves as an asset depends on its use in that context. CQU, Cestui Que Use: The explicit RE which benefits from work which can be performed on the type of thing the artifact is: the type or party that holds an objective purpose for this type of object and drives the most improvement in it. The CQU receives the join, holding the Operative Purpose that a Providing Element's Encounter Function serves. DE, Defining Element: The notable element of this AUE whose loss would prevent the AUE from remaining the same type. Its Encounter Function services the OP of a CQU outside of this AUE, names the functional type of the AUE as a converged result of the functionality of the AUE being examined. Its defining function is expressed independently of medium, encoding, genre, and style. SE, Substantial Element: An element whose Encounter Function helps the DE serve the CQU's OP. It counts as substantial because of what it is meant to contribute to this AUE, even when that contribution is subversive, weak, replaceable, or should be improved. NE, Notable Element: A component, interface, or specification that defines an essential demand or requirement. It is **notable** because it highlights what a system or component explicitly expects, needs, or depends on from its external environment to operate successfully.
element.name: Canonical Name (Project official terminology) or Informal Name
element.refs: Uniform dictionary shape for type-specific or artifact-specific keys
element.condition: Where intended functionality is absent, mark it `missing` (`MISS`). Where code is incorrect or not working, mark it `broken` (`BKN`). Where something appears not to belong, mark it `exclude` for examination.
element.note: record obvious concerns encountered during the trace so they can be examined. Identify the unique element type each concern belongs to and attach the finding with its references.

join.receiver: namespace address of the Receiving Element. RE, Receiving Element/Entity: The **who** or **what** bearing an OP. This is the element, person, group, system, component, or other participant with an Operative Purpose for the Encounter Function of an Element. The OP belongs to that receiver, and the join that records it lives in that receiver. Join: A dictionary object that exists in the Receiving Entity (RE) with a relation in active voice, an observation of the long lasting stable state of what is there; additionally it contains a dictionary of objects containing type specific or AUE specific references and logic.
join.provider: namespace address of the Providing Element. PE, Providing Element: The part satisfying the requirement actively declared by its CQU through its Operative Purpose. This is the join's other endpoint: whatever's EF fulfills the CQU's OP.
join.purpose: State the objective or standard this element or action fulfills. OP, Operative Purpose: The **why**. This is the active goal held in a CQU's join dictionary — that an element's encounter function intends to accomplish.
join.ef: Encounter Function of the PE within the RE context. EF, Encounter Function: The **how** of what is delivered. This may be understood as the function of an encounter or the encounter of a function depending on the contextual understanding of the Artifact. This is the mechanism, interface, relationship, or method through which an AUE or Element performs its purpose for its CQU. It explains how the effect is encountered, used, or experienced. The EF belongs to the Providing Element, but is stored in the CQU-owned join because a PE element type's functionality on the whole may satisfy different Vested Entities' Operative Purposes through different Encounter Functions. Record the PE's EF for that specific encounter in the join; do not create a single element-level EF record outside its joins.
join.perspective: Function if it is the encounter of a functionality, or Encounter if it is the functionality of the encounter
join.ifd: IFD, Information Flow Direction: the primary flow of information. sends: OP to EF. receives: EF to OP. both: equal need.
join.relation: Active-voice descriptive fragment starting with a third-person singular present-tense verb ending in -s/-es; the implicit subject is the PE if perspective is Function, or the RE if perspective is Encounter
join.verb: The single root verb extracted from the relation (e.g., provides, tracks, restricts)
join.observation: Only high-value observations consisting of long-lasting, stable state for agent orientation
join.non_goal: high-value non-goals consisting of structural constraints
join.refs: Uniform dictionary shape for type-specific or artifact-specific keys
join.condition: Where intended functionality is absent, mark it `missing` (`MISS`). Where code is incorrect or not working, mark it `broken` (`BKN`). Where something appears not to belong, mark it `exclude` for examination.
join.note: record obvious concerns encountered during the trace so they can be examined. Identify the unique element type each concern belongs to and attach the finding with its references.
